- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- The function/method name and approximate line

Be exhaustive. Report all distinct sites you find with concrete file paths and code snippets.

Based on my investigation, here is the answer.

h15.
Core memo read access (GetMemo, gRPC/REST API v1) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (`checkMemoReadAccess`, ~line 55)
ListMemos visibility filtering (anonymous → PUBLIC only; authenticated → own + PUBLIC/PROTECTED) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (`ListMemos`, ~line 219)
RSS feeds (explore + per-user) restricted to PUBLIC memos — `server/router/rss/rss.go` (`GetExploreRSS` ~line 90, `GetUserRSS` ~line 141)
Fileserver attachment/blob serving checks parent memo visibility — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (`checkAttachmentPermission`, ~lines 677/699)
API v1 attachment binary access checks parent memo visibility — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` (`checkAttachmentAccess`, ~lines 445/451)
ListMemoAttachments checks parent memo visibility — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go` (`ListMemoAttachments`, ~lines 214/222)
Reactions viewing/listing checks parent memo visibility — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (~lines 30/38/83)
Frontend SSR metadata/sitemap restricted to PUBLIC memos — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go` (~line 150)

The three most central "who may view a memo" sites are the API read path (`memo_service.go`), the RSS surface (`rss.go`), and the attachment-serving surfaces (`fileserver.go` / `attachment_service.go`), each independently re-deriving the PUBLIC / PROTECTED / PRIVATE rules rather than sharing a single ACL helper.

Note: a background search agent is still running; the sites above are confirmed directly from the source. I can fold in anything additional it surfaces if you'd like.

## Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites (usememos/memos, Go server)

Visibility values are defined in `store/memo.go:12-24` (`Public` = "PUBLIC", `Protected` = "PROTECTED", `Private` = "PRIVATE"). Enforcement happens at two conceptual layers: (A) per-memo ACL checks on an already-fetched memo, and (B) query-level filters that constrain which memos come back from the store. Below are all distinct sites.

### The three canonical enforcement surfaces
These are the primary "who may view a memo" gates across different server surfaces:

**1. Single-memo read ACL helper (gRPC/REST GetMemo path)**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`
- Function: `checkMemoReadAccess`, line 39
- The central ACL helper. Archived memos only visible to creator (line 45-53); non-public memos require an authenticated user (line 55-62); `Private` requires `memo.CreatorID == user.ID` (line 63-64). Called by `GetMemo` (line 356, and again for the parent memo at 367), `ListMemoComments` (line 148), etc.

**2. RSS / feed endpoints**
- File: `server/router/rss/rss.go`
- `GetExploreRSS` (line 72) forces `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` at line 90
- `GetUserRSS` (line 111) forces `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` at line 141
- Feeds only ever expose PUBLIC memos.

**3. Attachment/blob serving — parent memo visibility (file server)**
- File: `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- Function: `checkAttachmentPermission`, line 650
- For memo-linked attachments, fetches the parent memo (line 666) and gates blob serving on its visibility: PUBLIC served to anonymous only when anonymous access is allowed (line 677); valid `share_token` fallback (line 684-689); `Private` requires creator or admin (line 699-701). Unlinked attachments require the creator (line 652-663).

### Additional distinct enforcement sites

**4. ListMemos query-level visibility filter (gRPC/REST)**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`
- Function: `ListMemos`, lines 218-227
- Anonymous → `VisibilityList = [Public]`; authenticated listing all → CEL filter `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`; listing another user → `[Public, Protected]`. Archived branch restricts to creator (lines 188-195).

**5. Attachment GetAttachment ACL (gRPC/REST, separate from file server)**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`
- Helper: `checkAttachmentAccess`, line 422 (called by `GetAttachment` at line 256). Fetches parent memo (line 437); PUBLIC allowed (445); `Private` requires creator or superuser (line 451-452). Note this is a distinct implementation from the fileserver's check (#3).

**6. ListMemoAttachments visibility check**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`
- Function: `ListMemoAttachments`, lines 213-225 — same non-public/private-creator pattern before listing a memo's attachments.

**7. Reaction service visibility checks**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`
- `ListMemoReactions` (line 30-41) and `UpsertMemoReaction` (line 83) both gate on parent memo visibility (private → creator/superuser).

**8. Comment creation + comment listing filter**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`
- `CreateMemoComment` line 41: rejects commenting on a private memo unless creator/superuser.
- `ListMemoComments` lines 156-161: builds a `MemoFilter` CEL string (`visibility == "PUBLIC"` for anon, or `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`) passed to `ListMemoRelations` — plus the `checkMemoReadAccess` gate at line 148.

**9. User stats query-level visibility filters**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`
- Lines 83-91 (ListAllUserStats) and lines ~218-220 (a second stats path) apply the same `VisibilityList` / CEL filter logic as ListMemos.

**10. Markdown mention / embedded-memo reference resolution**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`
- `canUserAccessMentionContext`, line 56 — when resolving `@mention`/referenced-memo notification targets, checks `relatedMemo.Visibility == Private` (line 62) and `memo.Visibility == Private` (line 67) against the target user ID, so a mentioned user isn't granted context to a private memo they can't see.

**11. Share-token bypass path (GetMemoByShare)**
- File: `server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go`
- `GetMemoByShare`, line 153 — deliberately serves a memo regardless of visibility when a valid, non-expired share token resolves (via `getActiveMemoShare`/`isMemoShareExpired`, lines 195-208), rejecting only archived/missing memos. This is the sanctioned bypass of the visibility gate.

### Store / SQL query-builder layer (where filters become SQL)
The `VisibilityList` and CEL `Filters` set by the handlers above are turned into actual SQL WHERE clauses here (three DB dialects, identical logic):

**12. Direct `VisibilityList` → `visibility IN (...)` clause**
- `store/db/sqlite/memo.go` lines 96-102 (`listMemos`); mirrored in `store/db/postgres/memo.go` and `store/db/mysql/memo.go`.

**13. CEL filter compilation → SQL (handles `visibility in [...]` / `creator_id == ...`)**
- `store/db/sqlite/memo.go` line 61: `filter.AppendConditions(ctx, engine, find.Filters, ...)` compiles the CEL visibility filters from ListMemos/stats into SQL. Mirrored in postgres/mysql builders.
- Comment-listing variant: `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go` line 80-85 compiles the `MemoFilter` CEL string via `engine.CompileToStatement`.

### Note (not a view gate, but visibility-aware)
- `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` line 309 checks `memo.Visibility == store.Private` when deciding notification delivery — access-adjacent, not a memo-view enforcement point. Write-side owner/superuser checks (`UpdateMemo` line 426, `DeleteMemo` line 541) are also not view gates.

Summary: the enforcement is layered — per-memo ACL helpers (`checkMemoReadAccess`, `checkAttachmentAccess`, `checkAttachmentPermission`) guard single-object reads, while query-level `VisibilityList`/CEL `Filters` (set in ListMemos, RSS, stats, comment listing) are compiled into SQL in the store builders (#12/#13). There are two separate attachment-visibility implementations (gRPC `checkAttachmentAccess` and fileserver `checkAttachmentPermission`), and the share-token path is the one intentional bypass.</result>
